subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: Should gh-issues be considered fixed only after OpenClaw has both a runtime untrusted-content boundary for issue/comment text and accepted per-spawn child tool scoping?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent fix defines a security/API boundary across skill prompt construction, sessions_spawn policy, durable child-session state, and SECURITY.md vulnerability-versus-hardening semantics.

options.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
options.body: Land or replace the per-spawn tool-scoping work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length bounding, or equivalent runtime isolation before closing this issue.

options.title: Accept prompt-only hardening
options.body: Treat prompt guidance and global subagent policy as sufficient defense-in-depth while documenting that hostile issue bodies remain inside the operator-granted agent trust boundary.

options.title: Defer to unified delegation design
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers design one delegated-agent content and capability policy covering skills, hooks, cron, and sessions_spawn.

recommendation.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
recommendation.body: Land or replace the per-spawn tool-scoping work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length bounding, or equivalent runtime isolation before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined source/history signal across gh-issues, sessions_spawn, sandbox inheritance, external-content hardening, and prior maintainer-facing review context.
